ing: or minced scotch bonnet, to taste
st: Mix the flour, yeast, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[1 tsp]] cumin, sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt. Add the warm water and knead for 5 minutes into a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and let rise for [[1 hour]] until puffy.
For the channa, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot. Cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Mix the curry powder with a splash of water to make a paste. Stir it into the pot and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] salt and the water. Simmer for 25 minutes, mashing some chickpeas, until thick.
Heat the frying oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C). Oil your hands and pinch off golf-ball pieces of dough.
Stretch each piece into a thin 5-inch round and fry 30 to 40 seconds per side until puffed and pale golden. Drain on paper towels.
For each double, lay one bara on a plate, spoon on the channa and hot sauce, and top with a second bara.
Cut the shark into finger-wide strips. Toss with the juice of 2 limes, [[2 cloves]] garlic, thyme, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Marinate for [[30 minutes]].
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, baking powder, sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt. Add water slowly to make a soft dough, kneading for 5 minutes.
Cover the dough and rest it for [[20 minutes]].
Divide into 4 balls and flatten each into a 6-inch round. Heat the oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry each bake for about 1 minute per side until puffed and golden. Drain on paper towels.
Pat the fish dry and dredge in [[0.5 cup]] flour. Fry in batches for 3 minutes until golden and cooked through. Drain.
Stir the mayonnaise with [[2 cloves]] garlic and cilantro for a quick sauce.
Split each bake open, fill with lettuce, tomato and fish, and top with the sauce and a squeeze of lime.

ing: whole scotch bonnet or habanero, optional
st: Season the chicken with the soy sauce, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, the pepper and half the garlic. Rest for [[20 minutes]].
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the sugar and let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes until dark amber.
Add the chicken at once and stir to coat. Brown for 8 minutes.
Add the onion, remaining garlic and carrots. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add the pigeon peas, rice, thyme and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and broth, and tuck the whole pepper on top. Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly, lower the heat, and cook for 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest covered for 10 minutes, remove the pepper, fluff with a fork and serve.

ing: or fresh spinach plus a handful of collards
st: Wash the leaves well and remove tough stems. Roughly chop.
Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the squash, okra, broth, thyme and the whole pepper. Bring to a boil.
Add the leaves and salt, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until the squash is soft.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer 10 minutes more, without letting the pepper break.
Take out the pepper and thyme stems.
Blend with an immersion blender or swizzle stick until smooth and creamy. Season with black pepper and salt.

ing: cooked yellow split peas, for dhal puri
st: Simmer the split peas in [[3 cups]] water for 30 minutes until soft. Drain well, then mash to a dry paste.
Stir the cumin, garlic and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into the mashed peas.
Mix the flour, baking powder and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add the water slowly and knead for 5 minutes into a soft dough. Rest for [[30 minutes]].
Divide into 6 balls. Flatten each, spoon a heaping spoonful of the split pea filling in the center, and pinch closed.
Roll each ball out into a thin 8-inch round, dusting with flour.
Heat a flat skillet over medium heat. Cook the roti for 1 minute, flip, spread with butter and a little oil, and cook until brown spots appear.
Flip once more and cook 30 seconds. Clap the hot roti between your hands to soften it, then wrap in a towel.
Rinse the goat with the lime juice and water, then pat dry.
Rub the meat with [[2 tbsp]] curry powder, half the garlic, the cumin, thyme and salt. Marinate for [[1 hour]] or overnight.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add [[2 tbsp]] curry powder and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant.
Add the onion and remaining garlic and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the goat and brown for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Pour in the water and add the pepper. Cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until almost tender.
Add the potatoes and cook, covered, for 25 minutes more until tender and the sauce thickens.
Remove the whole pieces of thyme. Serve with roti or rice.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add warm water and knead for 6 minutes into a soft dough.
Cover and rest for [[1 hour]].
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until soft. Drain and mash.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil and cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes. Stir in cumin, curry powder and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, then mix into the potatoes. Cool.
Divide the dough into 12 balls. Roll each into a 4-inch round.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center, fold in half, and press the edges firmly with a fork.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry the pies for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with chutney or hot sauce.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar. Add the water slowly and knead for 6 minutes into a soft dough.
Brush the dough with oil, cover, and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Divide into 6 balls. Roll each out thin and spread with [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Roll each round up like a cigar, coil it into a snail shape, and tuck the end under. Rest 15 minutes.
Roll each coil out again into a thin 9-inch round.
Heat a flat skillet or tawa over medium heat. Cook the roti for 1 minute, flip, brush with oil, and cook until spotted brown.
Flip again, brush with oil, and cook another minute.
While hot, clap and crush the roti between two hands or beat with wooden spoons to shred it into soft strips.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Oil a baking sheet with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until crumbly.
Stir in the grated coconut.
Add the coconut milk a little at a time, mixing until a soft dough forms. Do not overwork it.
Knead for 2 minutes and rest for [[15 minutes]].
Divide into 6 balls and flatten each into a disc about 1 inch thick.
Bake for 25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown. Serve warm.
Rinse the dried sorrel in a strainer under cool water.
Put the sorrel, ginger, cinnamon, cloves and orange peel in a large pot with [[4 cups]] water.
Bring to a boil, then turn off the heat and cover.
Steep for at least [[3 hours]], or overnight, so the color and flavor get deep.
Strain through a fine sieve into a pitcher, squeezing the flowers.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved, then add [[4 cups]] cold water.
Add the rum if using. Chill well and serve over ice.
